justify_why_gaps_are_missing.justification: x-axis is time in days (0–4) with regular, consecutive integer tick marks; no portion of the domain is omitted.
y-axes show continuous quantitative scales (relative expression) with regularly spaced tick labels and no abrupt numeric jumps; no visual break markers are present or required.

flow cytometry plots use fluorescence intensity scales labeled along the x-axis (marker names). Tick spacing and axis labels appear continuous for the plotted range; there is no omitted region indicated that would require a break symbol.

y-axis (second fluorescence channel or density) shows continuous values/percentages with quadrant percentages annotated; no discontinuities or skipped numeric ranges are evident that would need an axis break.
x-axis encodes treatment conditions/concentrations as categorical positions along a continuous-looking axis; there are no omitted numeric intervals or jumps requiring a break mark.
y-axis shows percent positive cells from 0–100 with regular tick spacing; no abrupt numeric jump or omitted region that would require an axis break.
x-axis presents categorical treatment/concentration conditions; axis progression is continuous in presentation and does not omit numeric ranges that would need a break indicator.
y-axis is percent positive cells with standard 0–100 scale and regular tick spacing; there are no skipped values or discontinuities.
x-axis shows discrete population categories (1–8); categorical axis with no omitted numeric ranges.

y-axis displays normalized read counts with regularly spaced numeric ticks from low to high values; boxplots and whiskers extend within this continuous scale and no axis break symbol is present or needed.
heatmap columns represent samples/conditions (categorical labels); there is no numeric axis with omitted ranges that would require a break marker.

heatmap rows are gene labels and the color scale encodes numeric values; the colorbar is continuous (log2FC) and no axis discontinuity or omitted numeric interval is evident that would require a break marking.
